original_question: Can motivic integration for Deligne-Mumford stacks be developed over a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic and applied to the McKay correspondence?
target_in_paper: Problem 10.1 in §10 ("Generalization in various directions"): "Develop motivic integration for Deligne-Mumford stacks over a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristics and apply it to the proof of McKay correspondence over such a ring." ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it correctly identifies the two main tasks in Problem 10.1, namely extending motivic integration for Deligne-Mumford stacks to the mixed-characteristic complete-DVR setting and using that extension to obtain a McKay-correspondence result in the same setting. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
missing_details: The paper formulates this as a specific open problem (Problem 10.1), not as a broad research direction; the goal is to prove the McKay correspondence over the same mixed-characteristic complete discrete valuation ring, not just to "apply" the theory in some unspecified way. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The ambient base is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristics, with the paper's comparison point being the already-developed equal-characteristic theory over the power series ring k[[t]]; your draft does not indicate that this is a mixed-characteristic extension of that existing k[[t]] theory. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

The paper indicates that the main remaining nontrivial ingredient is the construction of the moduli spaces used in the theory, especially the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk (or variants thereof) in mixed characteristic. Your draft omits this key technical locus of the problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

Problem 8.2 sharpens the mixed-characteristic issue further: for a characteristic-zero local field K such as Q_p, the relevant moduli space should be defined over the residue field k rather than over K itself, and Witt vectors enter the formulation. Your draft does not mention the local-field/residue-field/Witt-vector aspect. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

In this paper, "the McKay correspondence" means the stringy-motive formulation of §2.3, namely the quotient-side stringy invariant/stringy motive being expressed by an integral over the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk. Your draft does not specify which McKay-correspondence formulation is intended. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))

There are no hidden conditions here involving homogeneity, degree bounds, nilpotency, or quantifiers such as "for all sufficiently large m"; those kinds of parameters simply do not belong to this problem's formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
refined_question: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic (0,p), with fraction field K and residue field k. Can one extend the existing motivic integration theory for Deligne-Mumford stacks from the equal-characteristic base k[[t]] to Deligne-Mumford stacks over R, in a form strong enough to prove the corresponding mixed-characteristic wild McKay correspondence in the sense of §2.3—namely, the stringy-motive identity relating the quotient side to an integral over the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk—especially by constructing the required mixed-characteristic moduli spaces of G-torsors (or their variants), which in the local-field formulation should be defined over k rather than over K as in Problem 8.2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Problem 10.1 and is close to it almost verbatim. The nearby discussion in §10 explains the exact scope: this is a further generalization from Sebag's motivic integration for formal schemes over complete DVRs and Yasuda's motivic integration for (formal) Deligne-Mumford stacks over k[[t]], with the aim of proving a McKay correspondence over a mixed-characteristic complete DVR. The same paragraph explicitly says that the remaining nontrivial issue seems to be construction of the relevant moduli spaces, pointing in particular to Problem 8.2. Section 8 then clarifies that, for a characteristic-zero local field such as Q_p, the moduli problem should live over the residue field via Witt-vector geometry. Finally, §2.3 supplies the paper-specific meaning of "McKay correspondence": the stringy-motive/stringy-invariant formula involving the moduli space of G-torsors over the punctured formal disk. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2107.07073))
